question: Which correctly describes chiplets?
choices: A technology that connects several small chips, divided by function, inside one package so they operate as one system
A technology that uses an entire wafer as a single chip
A technology that solders chips directly to the board without a package
explanation: Chiplets replace one large die carrying every function with separate small dies for compute, I/O and so on, densely interconnected inside one package. Small dies are less likely to contain defects, so they yield better, and each function can use the most suitable process. Chiplets are widely used in server CPUs and AI GPUs. Using a whole wafer as one chip is wafer-scale integration, and soldering a bare die directly to a board is chip-on-board mounting.

question: Which correctly describes a TSV (through-silicon via)?
choices: Lateral wiring formed only on the chip surface
An electrode that passes through the silicon substrate in the thickness direction, connecting stacked chips vertically
A solder ball used as an external package terminal
explanation: A TSV (through-silicon via) is a conductor filling a hole a few to over ten micrometers in diameter drilled through the silicon substrate, electrically linking its front and back. It enables thousands of connections between stacked dies over far shorter distances than wire bonds, so it is used in 3D stacking, HBM and silicon interposers. Lateral wiring on the surface is ordinary multilevel interconnect, and solder balls are external terminals.

question: Which correctly describes HBM (High Bandwidth Memory)?
choices: A slow memory using a single layer of flash memory
An SRAM cache built into the CPU chip
A memory that stacks several DRAM dies with TSVs and achieves high bandwidth with a very wide bus
explanation: HBM stacks multiple DRAM dies with TSVs and connects to the processor over an extremely wide 1,024-bit data bus to achieve high bandwidth. HBM3, for example, runs 6.4 Gb/s per pin for about 819 GB/s per stack. It is used in 2.5D packages placed beside the processor on a silicon interposer and is found in AI GPUs and similar chips. It is neither flash memory nor on-chip SRAM cache.

question: Which correctly describes the role of the silicon interposer used in 2.5D packaging?
choices: A heat sink for cooling chips
An intermediate substrate on which several chips are placed side by side and connected at high density with fine wiring
explanation: A silicon interposer is a silicon intermediary substrate on which wiring of 1 µm or finer is formed using semiconductor back-end processes. Multiple chips, such as a processor and HBM, sit side by side on it and are connected with wiring far denser than ordinary organic package substrates, whose lines are tens of micrometers wide, can provide. The interposer connects to the package substrate through TSVs. It is unrelated to cooling parts or photomasks.

question: Which correctly describes hybrid bonding?
choices: A technology that enlarges solder bumps to improve connection reliability
A technology that connects using two wires at a time
A technology that directly bonds surfaces of copper electrodes and dielectric without bumps, enabling extremely dense connections
explanation: Hybrid bonding planarizes chip or wafer surfaces by CMP and directly bonds copper pads to copper pads and dielectric to dielectric simultaneously. Without solder bumps, connection pitch can shrink below 10 µm and down to a few micrometers, multiplying connections per square millimeter by orders of magnitude. First commercialized in stacked image sensors, it is spreading to processor–cache stacking and HBM.

question: Which correctly describes a feature of fan-out wafer-level packaging (FOWLP)?
choices: Redistribution layers extend beyond the chip edges, so external terminals can be placed over an area larger than the chip
Connections are made only by wire bonding
The package is always smaller than the chip
explanation: FOWLP embeds singulated dies in mold compound to form a reconstituted wafer, then builds redistribution layers that extend beyond the die edges. Terminals can spread over an area larger than the die, so even small dies get many terminals, and without a package substrate the result is thin. It is used for smartphone processors and similar chips. Connections use redistribution layers rather than wires, and the package is larger than the die.

question: Which industry-standard die-to-die interface aims to let chiplets from different companies connect to each other?
explanation: UCIe (Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express) is a standard for connecting chiplets within a package, announced in 2022 by a group of major semiconductor companies. It specifies everything from physical-layer dimensions and signaling to upper-layer protocols, aiming to make it easier to combine chiplets from different companies and processes. HDMI connects video equipment and Bluetooth is a short-range wireless standard.

question: Which is especially likely to be a challenge in 3D packaging, which stacks chips vertically?
choices: Chips are too light to secure
Temperature rise from heat generated by stacked chips, and removing that heat
explanation: 3D stacking shortens wiring, but stacking heat-generating dies traps heat and makes it hard to remove from inner dies. Heat per unit area rises with the number of layers, and heat must pass through multiple bonding layers and thin silicon to escape. Higher temperature degrades performance and reliability, so thermal design, such as placing the hottest die next to the heat sink, is critical. Wiring actually gets shorter.

question: Which correctly describes SiP (system in package)?
choices: Several chips and passive components are housed in one package to function as a system
All functions are integrated on one chip
A system is built with software alone
explanation: SiP integrates processors, memory, power ICs, passive components and more in one package so that they function as a single system. Compared with an SoC, which integrates everything on one chip, it readily combines parts made in different processes and can reuse existing chips, shortening development. It is widely used in products that demand miniaturization, such as smartwatches and communication modules.

question: In flip-chip connections, what is the main advantage of using copper pillars (Cu pillars) instead of solder balls?
choices: Bumps can be made larger to increase contact area
Bump pitch can be narrowed, and electrical and thermal conduction are also excellent
explanation: A copper-pillar bump is a copper post tipped with a small amount of solder. Because it does not melt and spread sideways like a solder ball, bump pitch can be tighter, allowing more terminals. It also maintains standoff height between chip and substrate, easing underfill flow. Copper conducts electricity and heat well, benefiting current capacity and electromigration resistance. Soldering is still required.

question: What is the wiring layer called that is formed on a chip or wafer surface to route electrode positions to the positions of external terminals?
explanation: A redistribution layer (RDL) routes wiring from a chip's pads to wherever external terminals such as solder balls should go, built from alternating dielectric layers such as polyimide and copper traces. It is used in wafer-level packages, fan-out packages and interposers, with line widths shrinking from several micrometers toward about 1 µm. STI is device isolation and the BOX layer is the oxide in SOI.

question: Which approach, instead of a large silicon interposer, embeds small pieces of silicon only at the chip-to-chip connection areas to achieve high-density wiring?
explanation: The silicon bridge approach embeds small silicon pieces in the package substrate covering only the connection regions between adjacent dies, forming fine wiring on them for high-density die-to-die links. Eliminating a large interposer under all the dies cuts cost and allows assemblies larger than the lithography field. Intel's EMIB is a representative example. Wire bonds or lead frames cannot reach this density.

question: Which is a correct advantage of glass substrates, being considered in place of organic materials for next-generation large package substrates?
choices: They are soft and easy to bend
They have high flatness and dimensional stability, making fine wiring easier to form
explanation: Glass has a flat surface, little dimensional change or warpage with temperature, and a thermal expansion coefficient that can be tuned close to silicon's, so it is expected to support fine wiring and dense through-glass vias (TGVs) even in large package substrates. Since organic substrates warp more as they grow, glass is being considered for large AI packages. Glass is an insulator and is rigid, not flexible.

question: What is the technology called that mounts optical transceiver components close to switch ICs and the like in the same package, shortening electrical wiring to reduce power?
explanation: As data-center traffic grows, the power spent driving electrical signals from switch ICs to front-panel optical modules has become a problem. Co-packaged optics place optical transceivers in the same package as the switch IC, shortening the electrical path to a few millimeters and reducing power and signal degradation. It is one form of optoelectronic integration. BGA and QFP are common package types.

question: Among hybrid bonding methods, which allows only chips judged good in test to be selected and bonded to the target wafer?
explanation: Wafer-to-wafer bonding joins entire wafers at once, offering efficiency and alignment accuracy, but it bonds bad dies along with good ones. Chip-to-wafer bonding places only tested, singulated known-good dies onto the target wafer, improving stacked yield and allowing dies of different sizes to be combined. Placing dies one at a time, however, makes it slower than W2W.

question: What are the bumps called, far smaller than ordinary solder balls, used to connect chips stacked with TSVs and to connect chips to interposers?
explanation: Microbumps are tiny bumps 10 to several tens of micrometers in diameter at pitches of tens of micrometers, used for the many connections between dies. They join HBM DRAM dies in stacks and chips to interposers, often by thermocompression bonding. BGA solder balls, by contrast, have pitches of about 0.4–1 mm. When even finer pitch is needed, hybrid bonding is used.

question: In AI GPUs, what is the main reason the GPU chip and HBM are placed side by side on one silicon interposer?
choices: To connect the chips over short distances with an extremely large number of wires, achieving very high memory bandwidth
explanation: Each HBM stack has 1,024 data lines, and several stacks add up to thousands, more than an ordinary package substrate can route. Placing the GPU and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer with fine wiring connects them through many short wires only millimeters long, achieving memory bandwidth of several TB/s needed for AI computation. The purpose is neither to add parts nor to reduce capacity.

question: In 3D NAND, which is a correct advantage of making the memory cell array and peripheral circuits on separate wafers and bonding them together?
choices: The manufacturing process always takes just one step
Each can be made with a process suited to it, and chip area can be reduced
explanation: Fabricating the memory array and peripheral CMOS circuits on separate wafers, each with an optimal process, then bonding them places the periphery under the array and shrinks the die. Since array formation involves high-temperature steps, separating them keeps peripheral transistors from degrading thermally, allowing higher performance. The two wafers can also be processed in parallel, shortening manufacturing time.

question: What is the material called that is placed between a chip and a heat spreader to fill microscopic gaps and improve heat transfer?
explanation: Even when two solids are pressed together, microscopic roughness means only a fraction actually touches, and air in the gaps conducts heat poorly. A TIM (thermal interface material) fills these gaps to improve heat transfer; types include greases, pads, phase-change materials and metals such as indium. It is a critical component for high-power processors. Underfill and mold compound protect joints and encapsulate.

question: What is the data transfer capacity that can be secured per unit length of chip edge called, emphasized as a performance metric for chiplet interconnects?
choices: Bandwidth density (transfer rate per unit length of chip edge)
explanation: Chiplets usually connect through terminals lined up along their edges, so how much data can cross each millimeter of edge (bandwidth density, in units such as Gb/s/mm) is a key metric. Energy per bit (pJ/bit) is also important, and in-package links can be about an order of magnitude more efficient than board-level links. FIT is a failure rate and process capability index a quality metric.

question: Which correctly describes the difference between 2.5D and 3D packaging?
choices: 2.5D places chips side by side on an intermediate substrate (such as an interposer), while 3D stacks chips vertically
2.5D stacks chips vertically, while 3D places chips side by side
There is no difference between 2.5D and 3D
explanation: 2.5D packaging places multiple dies side by side on an intermediary substrate such as a silicon interposer and connects them through its fine wiring. 3D packaging stacks dies vertically, connecting them with TSVs or hybrid bonding. 2.5D dissipates heat more easily, while 3D gives the shortest wiring. Combined structures are also used, such as 3D-stacked HBM placed beside a GPU in a 2.5D arrangement.

question: In HBM, what is the typical number of DRAM dies stacked in one stack?
explanation: HBM stacks 8, 12 or even 16 TSV-connected DRAM dies on a base (logic) die to form one stack. Since stack height is fixed by the standard, adding layers requires thinning dies to around 30 µm and thinning the bond layers, and thermal countermeasures are also essential. One or two dies would forfeit the benefits of stacking.

question: What is the concept called that integrates chips made with different manufacturing processes and materials into one package?
explanation: Heterogeneous integration combines chips made with different processes and materials, such as leading-edge logic, DRAM, analog, RF and photonic devices, into a single system using advanced packaging. Combinations that cannot be built optimally on the same wafer, such as DRAM and logic, can be brought together. It is attracting attention as a way to overcome the limits of monolithic integration, which builds everything on one chip.

question: Which correctly describes the typical TSV formation process?
choices: Form it simply by pouring in solder
Etch a hole by deep etching, form an insulating film and barrier layer, then fill with copper or similar
explanation: TSVs are formed by deep etching, such as the Bosch process that alternates etching and passivation deposition, to create holes with aspect ratios around 10 in silicon. Insulator, barrier and seed layers are deposited on the sidewalls, and the holes are filled with copper or similar metal by plating. The wafer is then thinned from the back to expose the via tips. Filling deep holes to the bottom without voids is the difficult part.

question: What is the main aim of manufacturing packages all at once on large rectangular panels instead of round wafers?
choices: To increase the number processed at once and improve area utilization, lowering cost
explanation: Rectangular panels pack square packages without waste and scale up more easily than round wafers, so many packages can be processed at once. A 600 mm square panel, for example, has about five times the area of a 300 mm wafer. Panel-level packaging is being developed to cut costs for fan-out and large AI packages. Controlling warpage and uniformity over large areas remains a challenge.

question: To stack chips with TSVs, approximately how thin are wafers ground from the back?
explanation: Dies stacked with TSVs are thinned to a few tens of micrometers to keep via depth manageable and the stack thin. Starting wafers are about 775 µm thick, so this is less than a tenth. Thin wafers crack and warp easily, so they are processed while temporarily bonded to carriers. Millimeters or centimeters would be thicker than the original wafer and defeat the purpose of stacking.

question: Which correctly describes the benefits expected from using chiplets?
choices: They always become cheaper and faster in every case
The best process can be chosen for each function, small chips raise yield, and designs are easier to reuse
explanation: Chiplets let each function use its best process, such as leading-edge nodes for performance-critical logic and mature nodes for I/O and analog. Small dies yield better, and the same chiplet can be reused across multiple products in different combinations. Die-to-die interfaces and packaging add cost, however, so chiplets are not always cheaper or faster, and design work is still required.

question: Which correctly describes the conditions required of the surfaces to be joined in hybrid bonding?
choices: Very high flatness and cleanliness at the nanometer level
A thick oil film on the surface
explanation: Hybrid bonding joins copper pads and dielectric surfaces directly without bumps, so the bonding surfaces must have sub-nanometer roughness and be free of particles and contamination. A single particle of about 100 nm can leave an unbonded void millimeters across. CMP, cleaning and a very clean environment are therefore crucial. Rough surfaces or oil films prevent bonding.

question: Which correctly describes the role of the base die (logic die) at the bottom of an HBM stack?
choices: It handles the interface between the stacked DRAM and the processor, as well as functions such as test
explanation: The HBM base die handles signaling between the stacked DRAM dies and the processor and includes circuitry for testing and repairing defective cells. It has traditionally been made in a DRAM process, but in the HBM4 generation there is a move to make it in a logic process and add customer-specific functions. It is neither decorative nor light-emitting.

question: For high-power AI packages, which is a correct example of cooling methods being considered and introduced?
choices: Do nothing and wait for natural cooling
Liquid cooling, such as flowing liquid through cold plates or immersion cooling
explanation: AI GPUs can dissipate from several hundred watts to over 1 kW per package, beyond what air cooling can remove. Because water carries far more heat than air, direct liquid cooling through cold plates and immersion cooling in dielectric fluids are being adopted. Waiting for passive cooling or insulating the package would let temperatures rise until the chip fails.

question: Which is a basic advantage of 3D packaging, which stacks chips vertically?
choices: Interconnects between chips become shorter, enabling higher speed, lower power and a smaller footprint
The manufacturing process becomes simpler and cost always falls
explanation: Compared with placing dies side by side and linking them through substrate wiring, stacking them vertically shortens the distance between dies to tens of micrometers. Signal delay and wire-charging power drop, many connections can be made across the whole area, and footprint shrinks. Challenges include heat buildup, process complexity, and the fact that one bad die can scrap the entire stack.
choiceNotes: Correct. Shorter interconnects are the biggest advantage.
Stacking makes heat build up more easily.
Processing becomes more complex, and cost does not necessarily fall.

question: What is the problem called in which the speed of supplying data from memory cannot keep up with improvements in processor compute performance, limiting overall performance?
explanation: Processor compute performance has grown rapidly, but bandwidth to memory has grown more slowly, so compute units spend more time waiting for data. This is the memory wall. It is especially severe for large AI models, which read huge numbers of weights for every computation, and advanced packaging that places HBM next to the processor, along with stacked large caches, are countermeasures.
choiceNotes: Limits from heat are a different problem, called the power wall and the like.
Correct. It is the problem of memory bandwidth limiting performance.
Moore's law is an empirical rule about the growth in transistor count.

question: Which stacking method, long used in smartphone memory and elsewhere, stacks multiple chips slightly offset from one another and connects each to the substrate with wire bonding?
explanation: In a stacked MCP, thinned dies are stacked in a staircase offset or with spacers, and fine wires connect pads along each die's edge to the substrate. Requiring no special processing like TSVs, it is inexpensive and widely used in memory products stacking NAND flash or DRAM, with NAND stacks sometimes exceeding 16 dies. Wires are long and limited in number, however, so ultra-high-bandwidth applications use TSVs or hybrid bonding.
choiceNotes: TSV stacking connects chips through electrodes that pass through the silicon.
Hybrid bonding joins electrodes directly to each other.
Correct. Each chip is connected by wire bonding.

question: In contrast to chiplets, what is the conventional approach called in which all the functions a system needs are built into one large chip?
explanation: Monolithic, meaning "single stone," refers to building all functions on one silicon chip. On-chip wiring gives advantages in performance and power, but yield falls as dies grow, and die size is capped by the lithography field of about 858 mm². Chiplets that split functions were adopted for these reasons. Discretes are single-device products.
choiceNotes: Discrete refers to products such as single transistors and diodes.
Correct. It builds everything into one chip.
Hybrid is a general word for combining different things.

question: Advanced packaging steps that use front-end-like fine processing at the wafer level, such as forming TSVs and fine redistribution layers, sit between the front end and back end. What are they called?
explanation: Advanced packaging performs TSV etching and filling, fine redistribution, bumping and thinning at the wafer level using equipment and techniques close to front-end processing. Because these steps fit neither the traditional front end (circuit formation) nor back end (assembly and test), they are sometimes called the middle end. Both foundries and OSATs are investing in this area, and their division of roles is shifting.
choiceNotes: Correct. These are the steps between the front end and back end.
Upstream process is a term used in software development and the like for requirements definition and design.
Final process is not a common category.

question: Which TSMC 2.5D packaging technology is widely used to place AI GPUs and HBM side by side on a silicon interposer and connect them?
explanation: CoWoS (chip on wafer on substrate) is a 2.5D packaging technology in which dies are mounted on a wafer-form interposer (chip on wafer), which is then mounted on a package substrate (on substrate). Interposers can now be several times the lithography field size, and CoWoS is widely used to connect AI GPUs with multiple HBM stacks. Surging AI demand made expanding its capacity a major challenge. InFO is a fan-out technology and EMIB is Intel's bridge approach.
choiceNotes: InFO is TSMC's fan-out wafer-level packaging.
EMIB is Intel's silicon bridge technology.
Correct. It is the 2.5D packaging widely used to connect GPUs and HBM.

question: Which TSMC fan-out wafer-level packaging technology became widely known when it was adopted for a smartphone processor in 2016?
explanation: InFO is a fan-out packaging technology that forms redistribution layers on a reconstituted wafer with dies embedded in mold compound, making packages thin and small without a substrate. Its adoption in 2016 for Apple's smartphone processors, in a PoP configuration with memory stacked on top, triggered the widespread adoption of fan-out advanced packaging. CoWoS is 2.5D packaging with an interposer, and HBM is stacked memory.
choiceNotes: Correct. It is TSMC's fan-out packaging technology.
CoWoS is a 2.5D packaging technology using a silicon interposer.
HBM is stacked memory.

question: Which is a challenge of wafer-on-wafer (W2W) bonding, which bonds entire wafers together?
choices: Because good and bad chips cannot be paired selectively, the yield after stacking drops to the product of the individual yields
Wafers can be bonded even if their sizes differ
explanation: Wafer-to-wafer bonding joins every die at once, with high throughput and alignment accuracy. However, it bonds dies regardless of which are good, so two wafers at 90% yield give only 0.9 × 0.9 ≈ 81% after stacking. It is therefore used for high-yield, same-size die pairs, such as memory arrays with peripheral circuits or image-sensor pixels with logic.
choiceNotes: W2W bonds with highly accurate alignment.
Correct. Bad chips cannot be excluded from the pairing.
Wafers of the same size are bonded together.

question: In 2.5D packaging, what is the main advantage of using an interposer made of redistribution layers (RDL) of organic dielectric and copper wiring instead of a silicon interposer?
choices: It can always form finer wiring than silicon
TSVs become unnecessary and no heat dissipation is needed at all
It keeps cost down more easily and makes large-area interposers easier to build
explanation: Organic RDL interposers avoid silicon wafer processing, so they are cheaper, more compliant and easier to scale up in size. Their thermal expansion is closer to the package substrate's, which also reduces joint stress. Their wiring pitch and density usually fall short of silicon interposers, however, so they are chosen per application or combined with silicon bridges only where high density is needed.
choiceNotes: Silicon interposers often have the finer wiring.
Heat dissipation does not become unnecessary.
Correct. Low cost and easy scaling up are the advantages.

question: Through the HBM3 generation, which is the data bus width per HBM stack?
explanation: Whereas a typical DDR DRAM module has a 64-bit data bus, HBM has an extremely wide 1,024-bit bus per stack, achieving high bandwidth even with per-pin speeds lower than DDR. Gaining bandwidth through width rather than speed also lowers energy per bit. So many wires cannot be routed on an ordinary substrate, requiring dense wiring such as a silicon interposer. The next generation, HBM4, widens the bus to 2,048 bits.
choiceNotes: Correct. A very wide bus yields high bandwidth.
8 bits is a very narrow bus, the opposite of HBM's character.
64 bits is the bus width of a typical DDR module.

question: When a TSV wafer is thinned to tens of micrometers and processed, which technique temporarily attaches it to a support wafer (carrier) to prevent cracking and warpage?
explanation: Wafers thinned to tens of micrometers crack easily and warp badly on their own. They are temporarily bonded with adhesive to glass or silicon carrier wafers, backside grinding and wiring are performed, and then they are released by laser, heat or mechanical means (debonding). With a glass carrier, a laser can pass through to decompose only the adhesive layer. It is a key technology for handling thin wafers safely.
choiceNotes: Wire bonding connects a chip to terminals with fine metal wires.
Correct. The wafer is handled while temporarily attached to a support wafer.
Reflow is the step of melting solder to make joints.

question: In fan-out wafer-level packaging, what is the wafer-like form called that is rebuilt by placing diced chips with spacing on a support and embedding them in resin?
explanation: In fan-out packaging, tested known-good dies are placed with spacing on a carrier and surrounded with mold compound to rebuild a wafer shape, called a reconstituted wafer. Redistribution layers can extend over the mold compound beyond the die edges, so terminals can cover an area larger than the die, and using only good dies avoids wasting yield. SOI and epitaxial wafers are front-end substrates.
choiceNotes: An SOI wafer has a thin silicon layer on an insulating film.
An epitaxial wafer has a single-crystal layer grown on its surface.
Correct. It is a wafer rebuilt by embedding chips in resin.

question: Which is a challenge of moving to chiplets?
choices: The area and power of interface circuits connecting chips, and the effort of assembly and testing, increase
Chips from different processes cannot be combined
explanation: With chiplets, connections that would be on-chip wiring in a monolithic design must pass through die-to-die interface circuits (PHYs), adding area, power and latency. Advanced packaging assembly, known-good-die screening and post-assembly testing are also required. Adoption is therefore advancing in large chips where the benefits outweigh these costs. Yield tends to improve, and combining different processes is an advantage.
choiceNotes: Correct. The burden of interfaces and assembly increases.
Splitting into smaller chips actually tends to raise yield.
Being able to combine chips from different processes is one of the advantages.

question: What is the main aim of products that stack a cache SRAM chip on top of a processor chip with hybrid bonding?
choices: To boost performance by placing a large cache close by without enlarging the processor
To raise the processor's supply voltage
explanation: A larger cache reduces memory accesses and boosts performance, but SRAM consumes a lot of area and no longer shrinks well with scaling. Stacking an SRAM die directly atop the processor adds several times the cache capacity over very short distances without enlarging the processor die. It improves performance in cache-sensitive workloads such as gaming. It has nothing to do with color or supply voltage.
choiceNotes: It is not for changing color.
Correct. Stacking puts a large cache close by.
It is not for raising the supply voltage.

question: Which method is used to make silicon interposers larger than the maximum area a lithography tool can expose at once (about 26 mm × 33 mm)?
choices: Exposing with wiring joined across the boundaries of multiple shots (stitching)
explanation: A single lithography exposure field (reticle size) is limited to about 26 mm × 33 mm (about 858 mm²). AI packages carrying a GPU and many HBM stacks need interposers several times larger. Stitching, which precisely joins wiring across the boundaries of adjacent exposure fields, produces interposers exceeding the reticle size. Bigger lenses or wire connections cannot solve this.
choiceNotes: Correct. Shots are joined to expose a large area.
Enlarging lenses is not the solution; the exposure field is fixed by tool standards.
Wire bonding cannot achieve the fine wiring density of an interposer.

question: Which correctly explains how copper electrodes are joined to each other in copper-dielectric hybrid bonding?
choices: Solder is melted to connect the copper
The copper is stuck together with adhesive
The dielectric surfaces are bonded first, then heating expands the copper so the copper pads press together and join by diffusion
explanation: In hybrid bonding, planarized dielectric surfaces (such as oxide) activated by plasma are bonded near room temperature, and a subsequent anneal strengthens the dielectric bond. The copper pads are recessed by a few nanometers; on heating, thermal expansion presses them together, and atomic diffusion merges them. No solder or adhesive is used.
choiceNotes: Not using solder is a defining feature of hybrid bonding.
No adhesive is used.
Correct. It combines dielectric bonding with copper expansion from heating.

question: In classifying TSVs by when they are formed, which approach makes TSVs after forming transistors but before forming the multilayer interconnect?
explanation: TSVs are classified by when they are formed: via-first before transistors, via-middle after transistors but before multilevel wiring, and via-last after wiring or from the backside after thinning. Via-middle is widely used because it keeps copper TSVs away from transistor processing at around 1,000 °C while making connection to the wiring straightforward.
choiceNotes: Via-first forms them before transistors.
Correct. They are formed between transistor and interconnect formation.
Via-last forms them after the interconnect or after thinning.

question: Which pair of typical pitches (terminal spacing) for chip-to-chip connections is most appropriate?
choices: Microbumps about tens of micrometers; hybrid bonding 10 µm or less
Microbumps about several millimeters; hybrid bonding about 1 mm
explanation: Solder microbumps must avoid shorts from spreading molten solder, so their pitch is typically tens of micrometers (around 20 µm at the finest). Bumpless hybrid bonding goes below 10 µm and down to a few micrometers or less. Connection count scales inversely with the square of pitch, so going from 40 µm to 4 µm pitch yields 100 times more connections in the same area.
choiceNotes: Correct. Hybrid bonding achieves pitches orders of magnitude finer.
Several millimeters is wider than ordinary solder balls.
100 µm or more is about the spacing of ordinary flip-chip bumps.

question: In manufacturing fan-out wafer-level packages, what is the problem called in which chips shift position because of resin flow or shrinkage during curing when they are encapsulated?
explanation: When forming a reconstituted wafer, mold flow and shrinkage during curing and cooling can slightly move the placed dies; this is die shift. Even a few micrometers of shift can misalign the fine redistribution layers with the die pads, so it is addressed through materials and process optimization and by measuring each die's actual position and correcting the lithography pattern accordingly.
choiceNotes: Electromigration is the movement of metal atoms in wiring caused by current.
Latch-up is a high-current phenomenon caused by a parasitic thyristor.
Correct. It is chip misalignment during encapsulation.

question: What is the main reason for setting a keep-out zone around TSVs where no transistors are placed?
choices: Because stress from the difference in thermal expansion between copper and silicon changes the characteristics of nearby transistors
Because the area around TSVs cannot be exposed
explanation: Copper's thermal expansion coefficient, about 17×10⁻⁶ /K, is more than six times silicon's, about 2.6×10⁻⁶ /K, so temperature changes during manufacturing leave residual stress in the silicon around a TSV. Stress alters carrier mobility, shifting the current and other characteristics of nearby transistors. A keep-out zone of several micrometers around each TSV therefore excludes sensitive devices.
choiceNotes: TSVs do not emit light.
Correct. Stress from the expansion mismatch changes characteristics.
The area around TSVs can be exposed.
